126	def find_sentence_starts(all_words):
127	    """Stage 1 (mechanical, no LLM): every word that begins a sentence is a candidate clip
128	    start. Real timestamps only - never guessed or LLM-generated."""
129	    candidates = []
130	    for i, w in enumerate(all_words):
131	        if i == 0 or is_sentence_end(all_words[i - 1]['word']):
132	            pause_before = 0.0 if i == 0 else max(0.0, w['start'] - all_words[i - 1]['end'])
133	            candidates.append({
134	                "word_index": i,
135	                "time": w['start'],
136	                "pause_before": pause_before,
137	                "is_topic_start": False,
138	                "is_scene_cut": False,
139	                "is_script_paragraph_start": False,
140	                "score": min(pause_before, PAUSE_SCORE_CAP),
141	            })
142	    return candidates

145	def snap_to_candidate(candidates, time, tolerance):
146	    """Finds the candidate nearest to `time` within `tolerance` seconds, or None. Used to tie
147	    an externally-derived timestamp (scene cut, script paragraph) to a real sentence-start
148	    candidate rather than ever inventing a new one."""
149	    best = None
150	    best_dist = tolerance
151	    for c in candidates:
152	        dist = abs(c['time'] - time)
153	        if dist <= best_dist:
154	            best = c
155	            best_dist = dist
156	    return best

159	def apply_boundary_bonus(candidates, timestamps, bonus, flag_name):
160	    """Snaps each external timestamp to its nearest candidate (if any, within
161	    SNAP_TOLERANCE_SECONDS) and adds `bonus` to that candidate's score, flagging it."""
162	    for t in timestamps:
163	        match = snap_to_candidate(candidates, t, SNAP_TOLERANCE_SECONDS)
164	        if match is not None:
165	            match[flag_name] = True
166	            match['score'] += bonus

172	def detect_scene_cuts(video_path):
173	    """Runs a single decode pass with ffmpeg's scene-change detection and returns a
174	    deduplicated list of cut timestamps. No LLM and no extra input needed - purely derived
175	    from how the video was actually edited (hard cuts plausibly mark real structural
176	    boundaries: end of an attempt, next level, etc.)."""
177	    cmd = [
178	        FFMPEG_EXE, "-hide_banner", "-i", video_path,
179	        "-vf", f"select='gt(scene,{SCENE_CUT_THRESHOLD})',showinfo",
180	        "-f", "null", "-",
181	    ]
182	    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
183	    raw_times = sorted(float(m) for m in _SCENE_CUT_PTS_RE.findall(result.stderr))
184	
185	    deduped = []
186	    for t in raw_times:
187	        if not deduped or t - deduped[-1] > SCENE_CUT_DEDUP_WINDOW:
188	            deduped.append(t)
189	    return deduped

196	def align_script_paragraphs(script_path, all_words):
197	    """Aligns an optional original script's paragraph breaks against the real transcript
198	    timestamps via sequence alignment - tolerant of retakes/ad-libs/reordering, since it
199	    finds the longest common matching stretches rather than requiring an exact match.
200	    Returns timestamps for confidently-aligned paragraph starts; anything not covered by a
201	    long enough match is simply omitted rather than force-aligned."""
202	    with open(script_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
203	        script_text = f.read()
204	
205	    paragraphs = [p for p in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", script_text) if p.strip()]
206	
207	    script_tokens = []
208	    paragraph_start_indices = []
209	    for p in paragraphs:
210	        paragraph_start_indices.append(len(script_tokens))
211	        script_tokens.extend(_tokenize(p))
212	
213	    transcript_tokens = [(_tokenize(w['word']) or [""])[0] for w in all_words]
214	
215	    matcher = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, script_tokens, transcript_tokens, autojunk=False)
216	    blocks = matcher.get_matching_blocks()
217	
218	    timestamps = []
219	    for p_idx in paragraph_start_indices[1:]:  # the first paragraph starts at t=0 already
220	        for block in blocks:
221	            if block.size >= SCRIPT_MIN_MATCH_WORDS and block.a <= p_idx < block.a + block.size:
222	                transcript_idx = block.b + (p_idx - block.a)
223	                timestamps.append(all_words[transcript_idx]['start'])
224	                break
225	
226	    return timestamps

229	def classify_topic_transitions(candidates, all_words):
230	    """Stage 2 (batched LLM): asks Gemma to flag which candidate starts read as a new
231	    topic/section (e.g. the next level in a challenge run) versus a continuation of the same
232	    thought. Gemma only ever refers to the numeric IDs we assign here - it never sees or
233	    returns a timestamp, so it can't hallucinate one. Mutates `candidates` in place."""
234	    for batch_start in range(0, len(candidates), TOPIC_BATCH_SIZE):
235	        batch = candidates[batch_start:batch_start + TOPIC_BATCH_SIZE]
236	
237	        snippets = []
238	        for c in batch:
239	            idx = c['word_index']
240	            before = " ".join(w['word'].strip() for w in all_words[max(0, idx - CONTEXT_WORDS_BEFORE):idx])
241	            after = " ".join(w['word'].strip() for w in all_words[idx + 1:idx + 1 + CONTEXT_WORDS_AFTER])
242	            focus = all_words[idx]['word'].strip()
243	            snippets.append(f"{c['word_index']}: ...{before} [{focus}] {after}...")
244	
245	        prompt = f"""
246	        Each numbered line below is a short excerpt from a video transcript, with the
247	        candidate word wrapped in [brackets]. For each numbered line, decide whether the
248	        bracketed word marks the START of a NEW topic or section (e.g. moving on to a new
249	        level, challenge, or subject) as opposed to a continuation of the same thought.
250	
251	        Return ONLY a raw JSON object with this exact structure:
252	        {{"transitions": [{{"id": int, "is_topic_start": bool}}]}}
253	
254	        Lines:
255	        {chr(10).join(snippets)}
256	        """
257	
258	        try:
259	            result = call_ollama_json(prompt, TOPIC_CLASSIFY_SCHEMA)
260	            by_id = {t["id"]: bool(t["is_topic_start"]) for t in result.get("transitions", [])}
261	        except Exception as e:
262	            print(f"Topic classification batch failed, falling back to pause-only scoring: {e}")
263	            continue
264	
265	        for c in batch:
266	            if by_id.get(c['word_index']):
267	                c['is_topic_start'] = True
268	                c['score'] += TOPIC_TRANSITION_BONUS
269

271	def compute_end(start_word_index, all_words, duration):
272	    """Extends forward from a clip's start: lands on the end of the first sentence at/after
273	    TARGET_CLIP_SECONDS (a soft, natural landing), but never past MAX_CLIP_SECONDS or the
274	    video's end, and never mid-word."""
275	    start_time = all_words[start_word_index]['start']
276	    target_end = start_time + TARGET_CLIP_SECONDS
277	    max_end = min(duration, start_time + MAX_CLIP_SECONDS)
278	
279	    last_word_end = max_end
280	    for w in all_words[start_word_index:]:
281	        if w['start'] > max_end:
282	            break
283	        last_word_end = min(w['end'], max_end)
284	        if w['end'] >= target_end and is_sentence_end(w['word']):
285	            return w['end']
286	
287	    return last_word_end

290	def select_clips(candidates, all_words, duration):
291	    """Stage 3 (deterministic greedy walk): sequentially picks clip starts, preferring
292	    topic-transition candidates within a lookahead window, falling back to the nearest
293	    available candidate otherwise. Clips are allowed - expected - to overlap, since a clip's
294	    end is free to bleed into the next clip's territory rather than cut short for a clean
295	    ending. Advancing by a stride shorter than the clip length is what produces that overlap
296	    and maximizes clip count."""
297	    clips = []
298	    pos = 0.0
299	
300	    while True:
301	        window = [c for c in candidates if pos <= c['time'] <= pos + START_SEARCH_WINDOW]
302	        if window:
303	            chosen = max(window, key=lambda c: (c['is_topic_start'], c['score'], -c['time']))
304	        else:
305	            later = [c for c in candidates if c['time'] >= pos]
306	            if not later:
307	                break
308	            chosen = min(later, key=lambda c: c['time'])
309	
310	        end = compute_end(chosen['word_index'], all_words, duration)
311	        if end - chosen['time'] >= MIN_CLIP_SECONDS:
312	            clips.append({"start": chosen['time'], "end": end})
313	
314	        pos = chosen['time'] + CLIP_STRIDE_SECONDS
315	        if pos >= duration:
316	            break
317	
318	    return clips

335	def format_ass_time(seconds):
336	    """Converts raw seconds into H:MM:SS.cs format for .ass files."""
337	    seconds = max(0, float(seconds))
338	    h = int(seconds // 3600)

344	def split_phrase_lines(phrase):
345	    """Splits a phrase's words into up to two lines, by word count only (never by rendered
346	    width), so the split is identical across every dialogue event for this phrase. That's what
347	    keeps the layout stable: since only the active word's color changes (never its size), no
348	    dialogue event for this phrase can ever wrap differently than another."""
349	    n = len(phrase)
350	    if n <= 2:
351	        return [phrase]
352	    split_idx = (n + 1) // 2
353	    return [phrase[:split_idx], phrase[split_idx:]]

356	def generate_ass_subtitles(words, start_time, end_time, output_file):
357	    """Generates the TikTok-style .ass file from Faster-Whisper word data."""
358	    clip_words = [w for w in words if w['start'] >= start_time and w['end'] <= end_time]
359	    phrases = []
360	    current_phrase = []
361	
362	    for i, w in enumerate(clip_words):
363	        current_phrase.append(w)
364	        word_text = w['word'].strip()
365	        is_max_length = len(current_phrase) >= 5
366	        is_end_of_sentence = is_sentence_end(word_text)
367	        next_start = clip_words[i + 1]['start'] if i + 1 < len(clip_words) else w['end']
368	        is_long_pause = (next_start - w['end']) > 0.5
369	
370	        if is_max_length or is_end_of_sentence or is_long_pause:
371	            phrases.append(current_phrase)
372	            current_phrase = []
373	
374	    if current_phrase:
375	        phrases.append(current_phrase)
376	
377	    with open(output_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:

381	        f.write("Style: TiktokStyle,Arial,120,&H00FFFFFF,&H000000FF,&H00000000,&H80000000,-1,0,0,0,100,100,0,0,1,8,3,2,40,40,110,1\n\n")
382	        f.write("[Events]\n")
383	        f.write("Format: Layer, Start, End, Style, Name, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Effect, Text\n")
384	
385	        for phrase in phrases:
386	            line_groups = split_phrase_lines(phrase)

388	            for i, active_word in enumerate(phrase):

412	def ffmpeg_filter_path(path):
413	    """Escapes a filesystem path for safe use as a filter option value (e.g. ass=...) in an
414	    ffmpeg filtergraph, where ':' and '\\' are otherwise parsed as syntax. Windows drive-letter
415	    colons must be backslash-escaped AND the whole value single-quoted, or ffmpeg's filter
416	    option parser splits the path apart (e.g. treating it as two positional arguments)."""
417	    escaped = path.replace("\\", "/").replace(":", "\\:")

443	def _wrap_title_lines(title, font, max_width):
444	    """Greedily word-wraps a title so each line's rendered width fits max_width, measured with
445	    the font's actual glyph metrics rather than an estimate."""
446	    lines = []
447	    current = ""
448	    for word in title.split():
449	        candidate = f"{current} {word}".strip()
450	        if not current or font.getlength(candidate) <= max_width:
451	            current = candidate
452	        else:
453	            lines.append(current)
454	            current = word
455	    if current:
456	        lines.append(current)
457	    return lines

462	    max_lines lines within max_height, measured with the font's real glyph metrics. Returns
463	    (lines, font, line_box_h, group_height)."""
464	    max_text_width = FRAME_WIDTH - 2 * TITLE_SIDE_MARGIN - 2 * TITLE_BOX_PAD_X
465	
466	    fontsize = TITLE_MAX_FONTSIZE
467	    while True:
468	        font = ImageFont.truetype(TITLE_FONT_PATH, fontsize)
469	        lines = _wrap_title_lines(title, font, max_text_width)
470	        ascent, descent = font.getmetrics()
471	        line_box_h = ascent + descent + 2 * TITLE_BOX_PAD_Y
472	        group_height = len(lines) * line_box_h + (len(lines) - 1) * TITLE_LINE_GAP
473	        fits = len(lines) <= max_lines and group_height <= max_height
474	        if fits or fontsize <= TITLE_MIN_FONTSIZE:
475	            return lines, font, line_box_h, group_height
476	        fontsize -= 4
477	
478	
479	def build_title_image(titles, output_path):
480	    """Renders 1-2 clip titles as a standalone RGBA PNG: each title word-wrapped and centered
481	    in bold Impact text, each line on its own semi-opaque rounded-rect black highlight,
482	    stacked top to bottom. This gets composited onto the video via ffmpeg's overlay filter
483	    rather than drawtext, since drawtext can't do rounded corners and its fontconfig
484	    font-name lookups don't resolve real installed fonts on this system."""
485	    max_lines = TITLE_MAX_LINES if len(titles) == 1 else 2
486	    per_title_budget = (TITLE_BOX_MAX_HEIGHT - TITLE_GROUP_GAP * (len(titles) - 1)) / len(titles)
487	    groups = [_fit_title(t, max_lines, per_title_budget) for t in titles]
488	    total_h = sum(g[3] for g in groups) + TITLE_GROUP_GAP * (len(groups) - 1)
489	
490	    image = Image.new("RGBA", (FRAME_WIDTH, int(total_h)), (0, 0, 0, 0))
491	    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
492	
493	    y = 0.0
494	    for gi, (lines, font, line_box_h, _) in enumerate(groups):
495	        for li, line in enumerate(lines):
496	            line_w = font.getlength(line)
497	            box_w = min(FRAME_WIDTH - 2 * TITLE_SIDE_MARGIN, line_w + 2 * TITLE_BOX_PAD_X)
498	            box_x0 = (FRAME_WIDTH - box_w) / 2
499	            draw.rounded_rectangle(
500	                [box_x0, y, box_x0 + box_w, y + line_box_h],
501	                radius=TITLE_BOX_RADIUS, fill=(0, 0, 0, TITLE_BOX_OPACITY),
502	            )
503	            draw.text(
504	                (FRAME_WIDTH / 2, y + line_box_h / 2), line, font=font, fill="white",
505	                stroke_width=TITLE_STROKE_WIDTH, stroke_fill="black", anchor="mm",
506	            )
507	            y += line_box_h
508	            if li < len(lines) - 1:
509	                y += TITLE_LINE_GAP
510	        if gi < len(groups) - 1:
511	            y += TITLE_GROUP_GAP
512	
513	    image.save(output_path, "PNG")
514	
515	
516	def render_clip(real_video_path, start_t, end_t, titles, subs_path, title_img_path, output_path):
517	    """Renders one vertical clip via ffmpeg. Returns True on success, False on failure (and logs stderr)."""
518	    build_title_image(titles, title_img_path)
519	
520	    filter_complex = (
521	        "[0:v]scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=disable,setsar=1,boxblur=40[bg];"
522	        "[0:v]scale=1080:1080:force_original_aspect_ratio=disable,setsar=1[vid];"
523	        "[bg][vid]overlay=0:(1920-1080)/2[composite];"
524	        f"[composite][1:v]overlay=0:{TITLE_TOP_Y}[with_title];"
525	        f"[with_title]ass={ffmpeg_filter_path(subs_path)}[final]"
526	    )
527	
528	    codec = "h264_nvenc" if USE_NVENC else "libx264"
529	    ffmpeg_cmd = [
530	        FFMPEG_EXE, "-y",
531	        "-ss", str(start_t),
532	        "-to", str(end_t),
533	        "-i", real_video_path,
534	        "-loop", "1",
535	        "-i", title_img_path,
536	        "-filter_complex", filter_complex,
537	        "-map", "[final]",
538	        "-map", "0:a",
539	        "-c:v", codec,
540	        "-c:a", "aac",
541	        "-shortest",
542	        output_path,
543	    ]
544	
545	    result = subprocess.run(ffmpeg_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
546	    if result.returncode != 0:
547	        log_path = os.path.splitext(output_path)[0] + "_ffmpeg_error.log"
548	        with open(log_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
549	            f.write(result.stderr)
550	        print(f"ffmpeg failed for {output_path}. See {log_path}")
551	        return False
552	
553	    return True
554	
555	
556	def process_video(real_video_path, filename):
557	    print(f"\n--- Processing {filename} ---")
558	    base_name = os.path.splitext(filename)[0]
559	
560	    # Create a dedicated workspace folder for this specific video
561	    workspace_dir = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, base_name)
562	    os.makedirs(workspace_dir, exist_ok=True)
563	
564	    cache_file = os.path.join(workspace_dir, f"{base_name}_data.json")
565	
566	    # 1 & 2. Load from Cache OR Transcribe + AI Select
567	    if os.path.exists(cache_file):
568	        print("Loading transcript and AI clip data from workspace cache...")
569	        with open(cache_file, 'r') as f:
570	            cache_data = json.load(f)
571	    else:
572	        duration = get_video_duration(real_video_path)
573	
574	        print("Transcribing audio with Faster-Whisper...")
575	        segments, _ = whisper_model.transcribe(real_video_path, word_timestamps=True, language="en")
576	
577	        all_words = []
578	        for segment in segments:
579	            for word in segment.words:
580	                all_words.append({
581	                    "start": word.start,
582	                    "end": word.end,
583	                    "word": word.word,
584	                })
585	
586	        print("Finding candidate clip starts...")
587	        candidates = find_sentence_starts(all_words)
588	
589	        print("Detecting scene cuts...")
590	        scene_cuts = detect_scene_cuts(real_video_path)
591	        apply_boundary_bonus(candidates, scene_cuts, SCENE_CUT_BONUS, "is_scene_cut")
592	        print(f"Found {len(scene_cuts)} scene cuts "
593	              f"({sum(c['is_scene_cut'] for c in candidates)} aligned to a candidate start).")
594	
595	        script_path = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, f"{base_name}_script.txt")
596	        if os.path.exists(script_path):
597	            print(f"Found script file for this video; aligning paragraph boundaries...")
598	            script_starts = align_script_paragraphs(script_path, all_words)
599	            apply_boundary_bonus(candidates, script_starts, SCRIPT_PARAGRAPH_BONUS, "is_script_paragraph_start")
600	            aligned = sum(c['is_script_paragraph_start'] for c in candidates)
601	            print(f"Aligned {aligned}/{len(script_starts)} script paragraph breaks to a candidate start.")
602	
603	        print(f"Found {len(candidates)} candidate starts. Classifying topic transitions...")
604	        classify_topic_transitions(candidates, all_words)
605	
606	        clip_windows = select_clips(candidates, all_words, duration)
607	        if not clip_windows:
608	            print("No clips could be selected for this video. Skipping.")
609	            return
610	
611	        print(f"Selected {len(clip_windows)} clips. Generating titles...")
612	        fallback_title = base_name.replace("_", " ") + "?!"
613	        clips = []
614	        for cw in clip_windows:
615	            excerpt = " ".join(
616	                w['word'].strip() for w in all_words if cw['start'] <= w['start'] < cw['end']
617	            )
618	            try:
619	                ai_title = generate_clip_title(excerpt)
620	            except Exception as e:
621	                print(f"Title generation failed for clip at {cw['start']:.0f}s, using fallback. Error: {e}")
622	                ai_title = fallback_title
623	            clips.append({"start": cw['start'], "end": cw['end'], "ai_title": ai_title})
624	
625	        cache_data = {
626	            "duration": duration,
627	            "all_words": all_words,
628	            "clips": clips,
629	        }
630	        with open(cache_file, 'w') as f:
631	            json.dump(cache_data, f)
632	
633	    clips = cache_data['clips']
634	    if not clips:
635	        print("No clips recorded for this video. Skipping.")
636	        return
637	
638	    filename_title = build_filename_title(base_name)
639	
640	    for i, clip in enumerate(clips):
641	        start_t, end_t = clip['start'], clip['end']
642	        ai_title = clip.get('ai_title', filename_title)
643	        if TITLE_SOURCE == "ai":
644	            display_titles = [ai_title]
645	        elif TITLE_SOURCE == "both":
646	            display_titles = [filename_title, ai_title]
647	        else:
648	            display_titles = [filename_title]
649	
650	        subs_path = os.path.join(workspace_dir, f"{base_name}_{i:02d}_subs.ass")
651	        title_img_path = os.path.join(workspace_dir, f"{base_name}_{i:02d}_title.png")
652	        output_path = os.path.join(workspace_dir, f"short_{i:02d}_{slugify(display_titles[-1])[:30]}.mp4")
653	
654	        if os.path.exists(output_path):
655	            print(f"Clip {i:02d} already exists. Skipping.")
656	            continue
657	
658	        print(f"Clip {i:02d}: {start_t:.0f}s-{end_t:.0f}s | Title: {' / '.join(display_titles)}")
659	        generate_ass_subtitles(cache_data['all_words'], start_t, end_t, subs_path)
660	
661	        print(f"Rendering clip {i:02d} via FFmpeg...")
662	        if render_clip(real_video_path, start_t, end_t, display_titles, subs_path, title_img_path, output_path):
663	            print(f"Finished: {output_path}")
664	
665	
666	# --- MAIN EXECUTION ---
667	if __name__ == "__main__":
668	    print("Loading Faster-Whisper model...")
669	    try:
670	        whisper_model = WhisperModel(WHISPER_MODEL_SIZE, device=WHISPER_DEVICE, compute_type=WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE)
671	    except Exception as e:

673	        print(f"Details: {e}")

Roughly the same total time, likely a bit **shorter** — not longer. Two effects mostly cancel out, with a slight edge toward faster:

- **Fewer clips overall.** Clip count scales with `duration / CLIP_STRIDE_SECONDS`, which went from `duration/30` to `duration/75` — about **60% fewer clips** per source video.
- **But each clip is longer to encode.** Average clip length went from ~60-90s to ~150-165s (roughly 2.2x longer), and the ffmpeg encode (boxblur + overlay + libass, the actual bottleneck per the comment in `processor.py`) scales with frame count/duration.

Multiplying those out: total *encoded video-seconds* across all clips for a given source video comes out to roughly `duration × 2.1` under the new settings vs. `duration × 2.3` under the old ones — essentially a wash, slightly in favor of the new settings.

On top of that, fewer clips means fewer fixed per-clip costs that don't scale with duration:
- Fewer Ollama title-generation calls (~60% fewer)
- Fewer ffmpeg process launches and title-image (PNG) renders
- Fewer `.ass` subtitle file writes

Those all add up in the new config's favor. And the slowest fixed step — Faster-Whisper transcription — runs once per source video regardless of clip settings, so it's unaffected either way.

Net: expect per-video processing to feel about the same or modestly faster, not longer, despite each individual clip taking noticeably longer to render.

Two things worth knowing before you kick it off, though:

**1. This will process all 32 shortcuts, not just new ones.** `processor.py` only skips a video if it finds a cache file at `output_shorts/<name>/<name>_data.json`. Since you moved everything into `output_shorts/Short Versions/`, the top level of `output_shorts` is empty — so it'll treat all 32 videos in `videos_in/` as brand new: the 12 you'd already done (re-transcribing and re-cutting them at the new 2-3 min length) plus 20 you've never processed before. That's almost certainly what you want, but it's a much bigger batch than last time — worth running in the background/overnight rather than waiting on it.

**2. Moving those folders broke your existing schedule.** I checked `queue_state.json`: all 132 already-scheduled clips (2026-07-19 through 2026-08-31) store an `mp4_path` pointing at the old `output_shorts/<video>/...` location, and `browser_post.py` uploads directly from that path (not the copy sitting in `ready_to_post/`). Now that I've got a new set of shorts, I want to find a way to auto-upload them. The simplest way would be to just manipulate my keyboard and mouse over multiple TikTok and Instagram browser tabs (each site should probably be a different file, or at least different function). However, this has the side effect of taking up one of my screens for at least a few minutes and the HTML being less accessible to check things beyond images of the screen (which the code can't do without an LLM), so it would be preferable to manipulate the HTML via Python if possible. What are the viable ways to approach this problem? Once we figure out the best method, we can define the steps needed for upload

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-10 22:39:57Z)**_

Quick clarification that changes the framing here: `browser_post.py` **already does DOM manipulation via Python**, not mouse/keyboard automation. Playwright's `set_input_files`, `page.locator().click()`, and `keyboard.type()` all go through Chrome's DevTools Protocol directly into the page — it's not simulating OS-level cursor movement or reading pixels, and everything about the page (DOM, network responses, text content) is inspectable in code, not just as a screenshot. So the "manipulate HTML via Python" approach you want is what's already running.

What you're actually running into is narrower: the browser window has to be **visible** (`headless=False`), which is why it eats a screen. That's deliberate in the current script — TikTok/Instagram fingerprint headless browsers more aggressively, and posting/upload endpoints are exactly the kind of sensitive action platforms watch for bot signals on, so being detected can mean a CAPTCHA, a shadow-restriction, or a flagged/banned account. There are three real tiers of solution, trading effort against risk:

1. **Keep Playwright, shrink the footprint.** Split into `post_tiktok.py`/`post_instagram.py` as you suggested, and try Chrome's modern headless mode (`headless=True`, same Chromium rendering path as headed Chrome, less detectable than old-style headless) reusing your existing logged-in profile — a resumed real session is less suspicious than a cold anonymous one, so it's worth just testing empirically. If it gets flagged, fall back to headed but push the window to a virtual desktop or run it off-hours so it doesn't sit on your actual screen.
2. **Official APIs — the "proper" fix.** Instagram's Graph API has a real Content Publishing endpoint for Business/Creator accounts (what Buffer/Later/Hootsuite use) — fully headless, server-side, zero detection risk. TikTok has a Content Posting API too, but until your app passes their audit, unaudited apps are restricted (posts typically land as private/self-only rather than public). More setup (Facebook Developer app, business account linking, possibly waiting on review), but it's the only option with no ban risk at all.
3. **Unofficial/private API libraries** (e.g. `instagrapi`-style reverse-engineered clients). Fully scriptable, no browser at all — but they violate ToS more directly than a real logged-in browser session does, and they break often since they depend on reverse-engineered, signed mobile API calls. Given you have a real following now, I'd avoid this one.

My recommendation: start with **option 1** since it's a small delta from what you already have and costs nothing to try — test whether modern headless mode survives login/upload without tripping detection, and split the file while we're at it. If that doesn't hold up, or you want zero risk long-term, option 2 for Instagram specifically is worth the setup since Meta's API is mature and well-documented; TikTok's is murkier until audited.

Want to go with the headless-Playwright-first approach, or would you rather invest in the official APIs from the start?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-13 03:11:28Z)**_

That's on TikTok's side, not the script — a login/verification attempt cap, most likely triggered by the password reset plus repeated login attempts (a brand-new automated browser profile logging in for the first time can also read as more suspicious to their fraud detection than your normal phone app). Nothing in `browser_post.py` caused this; it hadn't gotten past the login pause yet.

A few practical notes:
- **Don't keep retrying right now** — repeated attempts while it's already rate-limited typically extends the cooldown rather than shaking loose a new code. These caps are usually temporary (often resolves in 30 min–a few hours, sometimes up to 24h).
- Try logging into TikTok normally on your **phone app** first (not the browser) once the cap clears — that often re-establishes a good standing session before you attempt the browser login again.
- When you do retry the browser login, do it as a one-shot deliberate attempt rather than several rapid tries, since that pattern is exactly what trips these caps.

I'll leave the poster.py finishing touch (2026-08-31) and the browser_post.py test alone for now — no rush on either. Let me know when TikTok lets you back in and we'll pick it back up.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-13 03:18:15Z)**_

Cleared. To summarize what was actually going on and what's fixed:

1. **The real bug**: that Chrome window had been sitting open on the TikTok login screen for 2 days. Every retry was hitting the same already-flagged session instead of a fresh one — explaining why a new password and waiting didn't help.
2. **A second, real contributing issue**: Playwright's Chrome exposed `navigator.webdriver: True`, a standard automation fingerprint that TikTok's bot detection almost certainly checks. Fixed in `browser_post.py` by adding `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` to the launch args — verified it now correctly reports `False`.
3. **Profile wiped clean** — no more stale cookies/session state carrying forward any accumulated risk score.

You're set up for a genuinely fresh attempt now. Run:
```
python browser_post.py
```
It'll open a brand-new browser and pause for you to log into TikTok and Instagram by hand. Do it as one deliberate attempt rather than retrying rapidly if anything goes wrong — that pattern is what tends to trigger these caps in the first place. Let me know what happens.

10	# Dedicated Chrome profile just for this automation - kept separate from your everyday

12	# once. First run creates this folder and pauses for you to log into both accounts by
13	# hand; every run after that reuses the saved session automatically.
14	AUTOMATION_PROFILE_DIR = os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "browser_profile")
15	
16	TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL = "https://www.tiktok.com/tiktokstudio/upload?from=upload"
17	INSTAGRAM_URL = "https://www.instagram.com/"
18	
19	# Named selectors, kept together so a platform UI change only requires editing this block.
20	TIKTOK_LOGGED_IN_PROBE = "[data-e2e='upload-icon'], a[href*='/upload']"
21	TIKTOK_FILE_INPUT = "input[type='file']"
22	TIKTOK_CAPTION_BOX = "[data-e2e='upload-caption'] [contenteditable='true']"
23	TIKTOK_UPLOAD_DONE_PROBE = "[data-e2e='upload-caption']"

28	INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON = "div[role='button']:has-text('Next')"
29	INSTAGRAM_CAPTION_BOX = "div[aria-label='Write a caption...']"

31	PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000

34	def get_todays_entries():
35	    """Reads directly from ready_to_post/<today>/ rather than queue_state.json's stored
36	    mp4_path - that field points into output_shorts, which can silently drift out of sync
37	    with what was actually captioned (e.g. a clip getting re-rendered at a different length
38	    under the same filename). Each ready_to_post .mp4 and its matching .txt caption were
39	    written together, at schedule time, so reading from here can't mismatch."""
40	    date_dir = os.path.join(READY_TO_POST_DIR, date.today().isoformat())
41	    if not os.path.isdir(date_dir):
42	        return []
43	
44	    entries = []
45	    for filename in sorted(os.listdir(date_dir)):
46	        if not filename.lower().endswith(".mp4"):
47	            continue
48	        mp4_path = os.path.join(date_dir, filename)
49	        txt_path = os.path.splitext(mp4_path)[0] + ".txt"
50	        caption_text = ""
51	        if os.path.exists(txt_path):
52	            with open(txt_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
53	                caption_text = f.read()
54	        entries.append({"label": filename, "mp4_path": mp4_path, "caption_text": caption_text})
55	
56	    return entries
57	
58	
59	def launch_browser(playwright):
60	    return playwright.chromium.launch_persistent_context(
61	        user_data_dir=AUTOMATION_PROFILE_DIR,
62	        channel="chrome",
63	        headless=False,
64	        viewport=None,
65	        # Without this, navigator.webdriver reads True and Chrome is trivially fingerprinted
66	        # as automated - almost certainly why TikTok's login kept hitting a hard "maximum
67	        # attempts" wall even with a correct, freshly-reset password that worked fine in the
68	        # real app.
69	        args=["--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled"],
70	    )
71	
72	
73	def ensure_logged_in(context):
74	    """On a brand-new profile, nothing is logged in yet - open both sites and wait for you
75	    to sign in by hand. On later runs the saved session cookies mean we're already logged
76	    in, so this is a fast no-op check."""
77	    tiktok_page = context.new_page()
78	    tiktok_page.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
79	    instagram_page = context.new_page()

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-13 03:29:45Z)**_

All four issues addressed:

1. **TikTok captions not filling** — switched from `keyboard.type()` to `keyboard.insert_text()` for both TikTok and Instagram caption boxes. Both are React-controlled rich-text editors with hashtag-autocomplete popups; simulating individual keystrokes commonly races with those and drops characters. `insert_text()` inserts the whole string as one operation, which these editors handle correctly.

2. **Instagram "Create" not "Post"** — added a second click on a "Post" menu item after the Create flyout opens, before the file picker.

3. **Instagram square crop instead of 9:16** — added a click on the crop tool followed by selecting "Original" (rather than guessing at a "9:16"/"Portrait" label, since your clips are already rendered at 1080×1920 by `processor.py` — "Original" just uses that real aspect ratio directly, whatever Instagram happens to call it).

4. **Tabs opening slowly/inconsistently, only 2 of 3 Instagram tabs** — this is very likely a direct consequence of #2: without the "Post" click, each Instagram attempt was sitting and waiting the full 30s timeout for a file input that could never appear (since the flyout was still open, not the upload dialog), then failing. That explains both the "slow, seemingly random" pacing and probably why the run didn't get through all 3 before you stopped watching — tab-opening itself is inherently sequential in this script (each clip's upload finishes before the next one starts), but it shouldn't be *this* slow anymore now that the flow doesn't need to time out repeatedly.

One honest caveat: I don't have a live authenticated session to inspect, so the Instagram "Post" menu item and crop-tool selectors are my best-informed guess based on your description and known Instagram markup patterns, not verified against the actual DOM. They're written defensively (multiple fallback selector patterns each) but may still need adjustment. )

CLIP = r"D:\Video Project Folders\AUTO TIKTOKS\ready_to_post\2026-08-13\1_short_00_beating_wii_boxing_while_handc.mp4"
OUT = os.path.dirname(__file__)

INVENTORY_JS = """
() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(
  '[aria-label], [data-e2e], [role="menuitem"], [role="button"], [role="dialog"], [contenteditable], input[type=file]'
)).map(el => {
  const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
  return {
    tag: el.tagName,
    aria: el.getAttribute('aria-label'),
    e2e: el.getAttribute('data-e2e'),
    role: el.getAttribute('role'),
    contentEditable: el.getAttribute('contenteditable'),
    text: (el.innerText || '').slice(0, 40).replace(/\\n/g, ' '),
    visible: r.width > 0 && r.height > 0,
  };
}).filter(x => x.visible)
"""


def dump(page, name):
    try:
        data = page.evaluate(INVENTORY_JS)
    except Exception as e:
        data = [{"ERROR": str(e)}]
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
    try:
        page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.png"))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  screenshot failed for {name}: {e}")
    print(f"dumped {name}: {len(data)} visible interactive elements")


def try_click_by_text(page, *texts, timeout=8000):
    for t in texts:
        loc = page.get_by_text(t, exact=False).first
        try:
            loc.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=timeout)
            loc.click()
            print(f"  clicked by text: {t!r}")
            return t
        except Exception:
            continue
    print(f"  could not click any of {texts}")
    return None


with sync_playwright() as p:
    context = launch_browser(p)

    print("=== TikTok ===")
    tt = context.new_page()
    tt.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
    tt.wait_for_timeout(4000)
    if not _is_visible(tt, TIKTOK_LOGGED_IN_PROBE, timeout_ms=5000):
        print("WARNING: TikTok doesn't look logged in - skipping")
    else:
        dump(tt, "tiktok_upload_page")
        try:
            tt.locator("input[type='file']").first.set_input_files(CLIP)
            tt.wait_for_timeout(20000)
            dump(tt, "tiktok_after_file_select")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  TikTok file select failed: {e}")

    print("=== Instagram ===")
    ig = context.new_page()
    ig.goto(INSTAGRAM_URL)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(4000)
    if not _is_visible(ig, INSTAGRAM_LOGGED_IN_PROBE, timeout_ms=5000):
        print("WARNING: Instagram doesn't look logged in - skipping")
    else:
        dump(ig, "instagram_home")
        if try_click_by_text(ig, "Create"):

            dump(ig, "instagram_after_create")
            if try_click_by_text(ig, "Post"):

                dump(ig, "instagram_after_post_click")
                try:
                    ig.locator("input[type='file']").first.set_input_files(CLIP, timeout=10000)
                    ig.wait_for_timeout(6000)
                    dump(ig, "instagram_after_file_select")
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"  Instagram file select failed: {e}")

    context.close()
    print("DONE")

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-13 04:11:42Z)**_

Key finding: the `aria-label="New post"` icon is still there in the real DOM — so the selector itself wasn't wrong, it's something else causing Instagram to not click it, and my diagnostic script's text-based clicking helper doesn't work for icon-only buttons since there's no visible text (only an `aria-label`), which is a limitation of my probe script, not evidence the real selector broke. Also notable: **TikTok's page didn't register as logged in at all** in this check — worth seeing directly rather than guessing. Let me fix the script to always capture screenshots regardless of the login check, and use aria-label clicks properly for Instagram.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-13 04:11:51Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```python
import sys, os, json

sys.path.insert(0, r"D:\Video Project Folders\AUTO TIKTOKS")
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
from browser_post import launch_browser, TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL, INSTAGRAM_URL

CLIP = r"D:\Video Project Folders\AUTO TIKTOKS\ready_to_post\2026-08-13\1_short_00_beating_wii_boxing_while_handc.mp4"
OUT = os.path.dirname(__file__)

INVENTORY_JS = """
() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(
  '[aria-label], [data-e2e], [role="menuitem"], [role="button"], [role="dialog"], [contenteditable], input[type=file]'
)).map(el => {
  const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
  return {
    tag: el.tagName,
    aria: el.getAttribute('aria-label'),
    e2e: el.getAttribute('data-e2e'),
    role: el.getAttribute('role'),
    contentEditable: el.getAttribute('contenteditable'),
    text: (el.innerText || '').slice(0, 40).replace(/\\n/g, ' '),
    visible: r.width > 0 && r.height > 0,
  };
}).filter(x => x.visible)
"""


def dump(page, name):
    try:
        data = page.evaluate(INVENTORY_JS)
    except Exception as e:
        data = [{"ERROR": str(e)}]
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
    try:
        page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.png"))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  screenshot failed for {name}: {e}")
    print(f"dumped {name}: {len(data)} visible interactive elements, url={page.url}")


with sync_playwright() as p:
    context = launch_browser(p)

    print("=== TikTok ===")
    tt = context.new_page()
    tt.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
    tt.wait_for_timeout(9000)
    dump(tt, "tiktok_upload_page_v2")

    print("=== Instagram ===")
    ig = context.new_page()
    ig.goto(INSTAGRAM_URL)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(4000)
    dump(ig, "instagram_home_v2")

    try:
        ig.locator("svg[aria-label='New post']").first.click(timeout=8000)
        ig.wait_for_timeout(2000)
        dump(ig, "instagram_after_create_v2")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  click svg[aria-label='New post'] failed: {e}")

    context.close()
    print("DONE")

That's the smoking gun. There's a **"A video you were editing wasn't saved. Continue editing?"** banner sitting on top of the page — a leftover draft from one of our earlier interrupted test runs — that the script never dismisses. That's very plausibly why captions keep failing: the automation has been proceeding blind while this banner sits in the way. Let me check the exact element to target for dismissing it.

import sys, os, json

sys.path.insert(0, r"D:\Video Project Folders\AUTO TIKTOKS")
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
from browser_post import launch_browser, TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL, INSTAGRAM_URL

CLIP = r"D:\Video Project Folders\AUTO TIKTOKS\ready_to_post\2026-08-13\1_short_00_beating_wii_boxing_while_handc.mp4"
OUT = os.path.dirname(__file__)

INVENTORY_JS = """
() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(
  '[aria-label], [data-e2e], [role="menuitem"], [role="button"], [role="dialog"], [contenteditable], input[type=file]'
)).map(el => {
  const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
  return {
    tag: el.tagName,
    aria: el.getAttribute('aria-label'),
    e2e: el.getAttribute('data-e2e'),
    role: el.getAttribute('role'),
    contentEditable: el.getAttribute('contenteditable'),
    text: (el.innerText || '').slice(0, 40).replace(/\\n/g, ' '),
    visible: r.width > 0 && r.height > 0,
  };
}).filter(x => x.visible)
"""


def dump(page, name):
    try:
        data = page.evaluate(INVENTORY_JS)
    except Exception as e:
        data = [{"ERROR": str(e)}]
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
    try:
        page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.png"))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  screenshot failed for {name}: {e}")
    print(f"dumped {name}: {len(data)} visible interactive elements")


with sync_playwright() as p:
    context = launch_browser(p)

    print("=== TikTok ===")
    tt = context.new_page()
    tt.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
    tt.wait_for_timeout(6000)
    try:
        tt.locator("[data-e2e='local_draft_container'] button:has-text('Discard')").click(timeout=5000)
        print("  dismissed stale draft banner")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  no draft banner to dismiss (or failed): {e}")
    tt.wait_for_timeout(1000)
    try:
        tt.locator("input[type='file']").first.set_input_files(CLIP)
        tt.wait_for_timeout(25000)
        dump(tt, "tiktok_caption_stage")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  TikTok file select failed: {e}")

    print("=== Instagram ===")
    ig = context.new_page()
    ig.goto(INSTAGRAM_URL)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(4000)
    try:
        ig.locator("svg[aria-label='New post']").first.click(timeout=8000)
        ig.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        ig.locator("svg[aria-label='Post']").first.click(timeout=8000)
        ig.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        ig.locator("input[type='file']").first.set_input_files(CLIP, timeout=10000)
        ig.wait_for_timeout(6000)
        dump(ig, "instagram_crop_stage")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Instagram flow failed: {e}")

    context.close()
    print("DONE")

import sys, os, json

sys.path.insert(0, r"D:\Video Project Folders\AUTO TIKTOKS")
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
from browser_post import launch_browser, INSTAGRAM_URL

CLIP = r"D:\Video Project Folders\AUTO TIKTOKS\ready_to_post\2026-08-13\2_short_00_beating_angry_birds_space_with.mp4"
OUT = os.path.dirname(__file__)

INVENTORY_JS = """
() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(
  '[aria-label], [data-e2e], [role="menuitem"], [role="button"], [role="dialog"], [contenteditable], input[type=file]'
)).map(el => {
  const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
  return {
    tag: el.tagName,
    aria: el.getAttribute('aria-label'),
    role: el.getAttribute('role'),
    text: (el.innerText || '').slice(0, 40).replace(/\\n/g, ' '),
    visible: r.width > 0 && r.height > 0,
  };
}).filter(x => x.visible)
"""


def dump(page, name):
    data = page.evaluate(INVENTORY_JS)
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
    page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}.png"))
    print(f"dumped {name}: {len(data)} visible interactive elements")


with sync_playwright() as p:
    context = launch_browser(p)
    ig = context.new_page()
    ig.goto(INSTAGRAM_URL)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(4000)
    ig.locator("svg[aria-label='New post']").first.click(timeout=8000)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    ig.locator("svg[aria-label='Post']").first.click(timeout=8000)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    ig.locator("input[type='file']").first.set_input_files(CLIP, timeout=10000)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(6000)
    ig.locator("svg[aria-label='Select crop']").first.click(timeout=8000)
    ig.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    dump(ig, "instagram_crop_menu")
    context.close()
    print("DONE")

42	def get_todays_entries():
43	    """Reads directly from ready_to_post/<today>/ rather than queue_state.json's stored
44	    mp4_path - that field points into output_shorts, which can silently drift out of sync
45	    with what was actually captioned (e.g. a clip getting re-rendered at a different length
46	    under the same filename). Each ready_to_post .mp4 and its matching .txt caption were
47	    written together, at schedule time, so reading from here can't mismatch."""
48	    date_dir = os.path.join(READY_TO_POST_DIR, date.today().isoformat())
49	    if not os.path.isdir(date_dir):
50	        return []
51	
52	    entries = []
53	    for filename in sorted(os.listdir(date_dir)):
54	        if not filename.lower().endswith(".mp4"):
55	            continue
56	        mp4_path = os.path.join(date_dir, filename)
57	        txt_path = os.path.splitext(mp4_path)[0] + ".txt"
58	        caption_text = ""
59	        if os.path.exists(txt_path):
60	            with open(txt_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
61	                caption_text = f.read()
62	        entries.append({"label": filename, "mp4_path": mp4_path, "caption_text": caption_text})

64	    return entries

72	        viewport=None,
73	        args=[

81	            "--mute-audio",

96	    instagram_ready = _is_visible(instagram_page, INSTAGRAM_LOGGED_IN_PROBE)

101	        input("Press Enter once you're logged into both...")

107	def _is_visible(page, selector, timeout_ms=5_000):
108	    try:

115	def post_to_tiktok(context, entry):
116	    print(f"  TikTok: opening upload for {entry['label']}...")
117	    page = context.new_page()
118	    page.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
119	
120	    page.wait_for_selector(TIKTOK_FILE_INPUT, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS, state="attached")
121	    page.set_input_files(TIKTOK_FILE_INPUT, entry["mp4_path"])
122	
123	    page.wait_for_selector(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_DONE_PROBE, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS * 4)
124	
125	    caption_box = page.locator(TIKTOK_CAPTION_BOX).first
126	    caption_box.click()
127	    page.keyboard.press("Control+A")
128	    page.keyboard.press("Delete")
129	    # insertText (not type) - these are rich-text editors with hashtag-autocomplete popups
130	    # that keystroke-by-keystroke typing routinely loses characters to.
131	    page.keyboard.insert_text(entry["caption_text"])
132	
133	    print("  TikTok: filled in, left on review screen - click Post yourself when ready.")
134	
135

11	# Chrome profile because Chrome refuses to let two processes drive the same profile at
12	# once. First run creates this folder and pauses for you to log into both accounts by
13	# hand; every run after that reuses the saved session automatically.

28	TIKTOK_DISCARD_POST_BUTTON = "[data-e2e='discard_post_button']"

36	INSTAGRAM_POST_MENU_ITEM = "svg[aria-label='Post']"

49	def get_todays_entries():
50	    """Reads directly from ready_to_post/<today>/ rather than queue_state.json's stored
51	    mp4_path - that field points into output_shorts, which can silently drift out of sync
52	    with what was actually captioned (e.g. a clip getting re-rendered at a different length
53	    under the same filename). Each ready_to_post .mp4 and its matching .txt caption were
54	    written together, at schedule time, so reading from here can't mismatch."""
55	    date_dir = os.path.join(READY_TO_POST_DIR, date.today().isoformat())
56	    if not os.path.isdir(date_dir):
57	        return []
58	
59	    entries = []
60	    for filename in sorted(os.listdir(date_dir)):
61	        if not filename.lower().endswith(".mp4"):
62	            continue
63	        mp4_path = os.path.join(date_dir, filename)
64	        txt_path = os.path.splitext(mp4_path)[0] + ".txt"
65	        caption_text = ""
66	        if os.path.exists(txt_path):
67	            with open(txt_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
68	                caption_text = f.read()
69	        entries.append({"label": filename, "mp4_path": mp4_path, "caption_text": caption_text})
70	
71	    return entries
72	
73	
74	def launch_browser(playwright):
75	    return playwright.chromium.launch_persistent_context(
76	        user_data_dir=AUTOMATION_PROFILE_DIR,
77	        channel="chrome",
78	        headless=False,
79	        viewport=None,
80	        args=[
81	            # Without this, navigator.webdriver reads True and Chrome is trivially
82	            # fingerprinted as automated - almost certainly why TikTok's login kept hitting a
83	            # hard "maximum attempts" wall even with a correct, freshly-reset password that

93	def ensure_logged_in(context):
94	    """On a brand-new profile, nothing is logged in yet - open both sites and wait for you
95	    to sign in by hand. On later runs the saved session cookies mean we're already logged
96	    in, so this is a fast no-op check."""
97	    tiktok_page = context.new_page()
98	    tiktok_page.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
99	    instagram_page = context.new_page()
100	    instagram_page.goto(INSTAGRAM_URL)
101	
102	    # A generous timeout here matters - this fires right after a fresh page load, and a slow
103	    # first paint being mistaken for "not logged in" would demand a manual login that isn't
104	    # actually needed.
105	    tiktok_ready = _is_visible(tiktok_page, TIKTOK_LOGGED_IN_PROBE, timeout_ms=15_000)
106	    instagram_ready = _is_visible(instagram_page, INSTAGRAM_LOGGED_IN_PROBE, timeout_ms=15_000)
107	
108	    if not (tiktok_ready and instagram_ready):
109	        print("First-time setup: log into TikTok and Instagram in the two tabs that just "
110	              "opened, then come back here.")
111	        input("Press Enter once you're logged into both...")
112	
113	    tiktok_page.close()
114	    instagram_page.close()
115

117	def _is_visible(page, selector, timeout_ms=5_000):
118	    try:
119	        page.wait_for_selector(selector, timeout=timeout_ms, state="visible")
120	        return True
121	    except Exception:
122	        return False
123	
124	
125	def _dismiss_if_present(page, selector, timeout_ms=4_000):
126	    """Clicks selector if it shows up within timeout_ms; silently does nothing otherwise.
127	    Used for TikTok's stale-draft interruptions, which may or may not be there."""
128	    try:
129	        page.locator(selector).first.click(timeout=timeout_ms)
130	        return True
131	    except Exception:
132	        return False
133

135	def post_to_tiktok(context, entry):
136	    print(f"  TikTok: opening upload for {entry['label']}...")
137	    page = context.new_page()
138	    page.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
139	
140	    # Repeated test runs (or a previous run that got interrupted) leave an unsaved draft
141	    # behind, which TikTok surfaces as a banner and/or a "Discard this post?" dialog on top
142	    # of the upload page - clear either out before trying to select a file underneath them.
143	    _dismiss_if_present(page, TIKTOK_STALE_DRAFT_BANNER_DISCARD)
144	    _dismiss_if_present(page, TIKTOK_DISCARD_POST_BUTTON)
145	
146	    page.wait_for_selector(TIKTOK_FILE_INPUT, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS, state="attached")
147	    page.set_input_files(TIKTOK_FILE_INPUT, entry["mp4_path"])
148	
149	    page.wait_for_selector(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_DONE_PROBE, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS * 4)
150	
151	    caption_box = page.locator(TIKTOK_CAPTION_BOX).first
152	    caption_box.click()
153	    page.keyboard.press("Control+A")
154	    page.keyboard.press("Delete")
155	    # insertText (not type) - these are rich-text editors with hashtag-autocomplete popups
156	    # that keystroke-by-keystroke typing routinely loses characters to.
157	    page.keyboard.insert_text(entry["caption_text"])
158	
159	    print("  TikTok: filled in, left on review screen - click Post yourself when ready.")
160	
161	
162	def post_to_instagram(context, entry):
163	    print(f"  Instagram: opening upload for {entry['label']}...")
164	    page = context.new_page()
165	    page.goto(INSTAGRAM_URL)
166	
167	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_CREATE_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
168	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_CREATE_BUTTON)
169	
170	    # "Create" opens a flyout (Post/Reel/Story/...) - pick "Post" specifically.
171	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_POST_MENU_ITEM, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
172	    page.locator(INSTAGRAM_POST_MENU_ITEM).first.click()
173	
174	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_FILE_INPUT, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS, state="attached")
175	    page.set_input_files(INSTAGRAM_FILE_INPUT, entry["mp4_path"])
176	
177	    # Crop defaults to square regardless of the source video's real aspect ratio - switch it
178	    # to 9:16, which is what processor.py always renders.
179	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_CROP_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
180	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_CROP_BUTTON)
181	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_ASPECT_9_16_OPTION, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
182	    page.locator(INSTAGRAM_ASPECT_9_16_OPTION).first.click()
183	
184	    # Filters, then final details - two "Next" screens before the caption step.
185	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS * 2)
186	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON)
187	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
188	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON)
189	
190	    caption_box = page.locator(INSTAGRAM_CAPTION_BOX).first
191	    caption_box.click()
192	    page.keyboard.insert_text(entry["caption_text"])
193	
194	    print("  Instagram: filled in, left on review screen - click Share yourself when ready.")
195	
196	
197	def main():
198	    entries = get_todays_entries()
199	
200	    if not entries:
201	        print(f"Nothing found in {os.path.join(READY_TO_POST_DIR, date.today().isoformat())} - run poster.py first.")
202	        return
203	
204	    with sync_playwright() as playwright:
205	        context = launch_browser(playwright)
206	        ensure_logged_in(context)

208	        for entry in entries:

214	            try:

216	            except Exception as e:
217	                print(f"  Instagram upload failed for this clip: {e}")
218	
219	        input("\nReview each open tab and click post/schedule yourself, then press Enter to close...")

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-16 00:14:46Z)**_

Found it — my dismissal check ran too early; the "Discard this post?" modal appears with a slight delay (race condition), so a one-shot check before the click isn't enough. And the Instagram failure references a *different* stale draft each time, confirming a cascading pattern: each failed attempt leaves its own unfinished draft behind, which then blocks the next attempt. I need a retry-on-failure pattern instead of a single check. I also suspect the Instagram crop menu needs more settle time after file upload — my diagnostic script waited 6s there before it worked; the real script has no such wait.

113	
114	    tiktok_page.close()
115	    instagram_page.close()
116	
117	
118	def _is_visible(page, selector, timeout_ms=5_000):
119	    try:
120	        page.wait_for_selector(selector, timeout=timeout_ms, state="visible")
121	        return True
122	    except Exception:
123	        return False
124	
125	
126	def _dismiss_if_present(page, selector, timeout_ms=4_000):
127	    """Clicks selector if it shows up within timeout_ms; silently does nothing otherwise.
128	    Used for TikTok's stale-draft interruptions, which may or may not be there."""
129	    try:
130	        page.locator(selector).first.click(timeout=timeout_ms)
131	        return True
132	    except Exception:
133	        return False
134	
135	
136	def post_to_tiktok(context, entry):
137	    print(f"  TikTok: opening upload for {entry['label']}...")
138	    page = context.new_page()
139	    # With several tabs accumulating across entries, a page that never gets OS-level focus
140	    # can have its rendering throttled by Chrome's background-tab power saving - explicitly
141	    # foreground whichever tab we're actively driving.
142	    page.bring_to_front()
143	    page.goto(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_URL)
144	
145	    # Repeated test runs (or a previous run that got interrupted) leave an unsaved draft
146	    # behind, which TikTok surfaces as a banner and/or a "Discard this post?" dialog on top
147	    # of the upload page - clear either out before trying to select a file underneath them.
148	    _dismiss_if_present(page, TIKTOK_STALE_DRAFT_BANNER_DISCARD)
149	    _dismiss_if_present(page, TIKTOK_DISCARD_POST_BUTTON)
150	
151	    page.wait_for_selector(TIKTOK_FILE_INPUT, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS, state="attached")
152	    page.set_input_files(TIKTOK_FILE_INPUT, entry["mp4_path"])
153	
154	    page.wait_for_selector(TIKTOK_UPLOAD_DONE_PROBE, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS * 4)
155	
156	    # The same stale-draft dialog can reappear here, mid-flow, once THIS upload starts -
157	    # it's what was blocking every caption click with a "subtree intercepts pointer events"
158	    # error, since Playwright's own click-retry loop never thinks to dismiss it.
159	    _dismiss_if_present(page, TIKTOK_DISCARD_POST_BUTTON, timeout_ms=3_000)
160	
161	    caption_box = page.locator(TIKTOK_CAPTION_BOX).first
162	    caption_box.click()
163	    page.keyboard.press("Control+A")
164	    page.keyboard.press("Delete")
165	    # insertText (not type) - these are rich-text editors with hashtag-autocomplete popups
166	    # that keystroke-by-keystroke typing routinely loses characters to.
167	    page.keyboard.insert_text(entry["caption_text"])
168	
169	    print("  TikTok: filled in, left on review screen - click Post yourself when ready.")
170	
171	
172	def post_to_instagram(context, entry):
173	    print(f"  Instagram: opening upload for {entry['label']}...")
174	    page = context.new_page()
175	    page.bring_to_front()
176	    page.goto(INSTAGRAM_URL)
177	
178	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_CREATE_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
179	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_CREATE_BUTTON)
180	
181	    # "Create" opens a flyout (Post/Reel/Story/...) - pick "Post" specifically.
182	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_POST_MENU_ITEM, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
183	    page.locator(INSTAGRAM_POST_MENU_ITEM).first.click()
184	
185	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_FILE_INPUT, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS, state="attached")
186	    page.set_input_files(INSTAGRAM_FILE_INPUT, entry["mp4_path"])
187	
188	    # Crop defaults to square regardless of the source video's real aspect ratio - switch it
189	    # to 9:16, which is what processor.py always renders.
190	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_CROP_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
191	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_CROP_BUTTON)
192	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_ASPECT_9_16_OPTION, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
193	    page.locator(INSTAGRAM_ASPECT_9_16_OPTION).first.click()
194	
195	    # Filters, then final details - two "Next" screens before the caption step.
196	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS * 2)
197	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON)
198	    page.wait_for_selector(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON, timeout=PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS)
199	    page.click(INSTAGRAM_NEXT_BUTTON)
200	
201	    caption_box = page.locator(INSTAGRAM_CAPTION_BOX).first
202	    caption_box.click()
203	    page.keyboard.insert_text(entry["caption_text"])
204	
205	    print("  Instagram: filled in, left on review screen - click Share yourself when ready.")
206	
207	
208	def main():
209	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
210	    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None,
211	                         help="Only process the first N of today's entries (for testing).")
212	    args = parser.parse_args()
213	
214	    entries = get_todays_entries()
215	    if args.limit is not None:
216	        entries = entries[:args.limit]
217	
218	    if not entries:
219	        print(f"Nothing found in {os.path.join(READY_TO_POST_DIR, date.today().isoformat())} - run poster.py first.")
220	        return
221	
222	    with sync_playwright() as playwright:
223	        context = launch_browser(playwright)
224	        ensure_logged_in(context)
225	
226	        for entry in entries:
227	            print(f"{entry['label']}:")
228	            try:
229	                post_to_tiktok(context, entry)
230	            except Exception as e:
231	                print(f"  TikTok upload failed for this clip: {e}")
232	            try:
233	                post_to_instagram(context, entry)
234	            except Exception as e:
235	                print(f"  Instagram upload failed for this clip: {e}")
236	
237	        input("\nReview each open tab and click post/schedule yourself, then press Enter to close...")
238	        context.close()
239	
240	
241	if __name__ == "__main__":
242	    main()
243
```

Very revealing — the "9:16" option IS visibly present in this exact failure screenshot, yet `wait_for_selector` still timed out. That means `:text-is('9:16')` (exact match) is failing on some structural quirk — likely extra whitespace or a nested decorative element making the element's full text not *exactly* "9:16". I'll switch to a substring match (`:has-text`) instead, which is more forgiving. For TikTok, the screenshot revealed the real bug: there are **two** "Discard" buttons on screen — the modal's confirm button *and* a separate page-level "Discard" button in the bottom action bar — and my selector was almost certainly matching the wrong (obscured, page-level) one, causing the dismiss click to fail silently.

import os, re
from datetime import date, timedelta

today = date.today()
date_dirs = sorted(d for d in os.listdir('.') if re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', d))
earliest = date.fromisoformat(date_dirs[0])
offset = (today - earliest).days
print(f'Today: {today}, Earliest folder: {earliest}, Offset: {offset} days')
print(f'{len(date_dirs)} date folders to shift:', date_dirs[0], '..', date_dirs[-1])

# Descending order so each target is vacated by an earlier iteration before we need it
# (target = source + offset, and larger sources are processed first).
for d in sorted(date_dirs, reverse=True):
    src_date = date.fromisoformat(d)
    dst = (src_date + timedelta(days=offset)).isoformat()
    print(f'{d} -> {dst}')
    os.rename(d, dst)

print('Done.')
"

38	# videos whose local shortcut name has drifted from the real YouTube title (e.g. renamed
39	# for a better clip title). One per line: "Exact Local Name = https://youtu.be/xxxx".
40	# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. Most videos won't need an entry here.
41	YOUTUBE_OVERRIDES_FILE = os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "youtube_url_overrides.txt")
42	
43	os.makedirs(READY_TO_POST_DIR, exist_ok=True)
44	
45	YOUTUBE_API_BASE = "https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3"
46	
47	CAPTION_SCHEMA = {
48	    "type": "object",
49	    "properties": {
50	        "hashtags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
51	    },
52	    "required": ["hashtags"],
53	}
54	
55	
56	def game_hashtag(source_video_title):
57	    """Returns the established franchise hashtag for a source video's game, or None if it
58	    doesn't match anything in GAME_HASHTAGS."""
59	    lowered = source_video_title.lower()
60	    for keyword, hashtag in GAME_HASHTAGS:
61	        if keyword in lowered:
62	            return hashtag
63	    return None
64	
65	
66	def fetch_youtube_video_map():
67	    """Returns {video_title: video_url} for the whole channel. Cached locally (refreshed
68	    once a day) so this doesn't hit the API on every run."""
69	    if os.path.exists(YOUTUBE_CACHE_FILE):
70	        age = time.time() - os.path.getmtime(YOUTUBE_CACHE_FILE)
71	        if age < YOUTUBE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:
72	            with open(YOUTUBE_CACHE_FILE, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
73	                return json.load(f)
74	
75	    if not YOUTUBE_API_KEY or "PUT_YOUR" in YOUTUBE_API_KEY:
76	        print("WARNING: YOUTUBE_API_KEY isn't set in poster.py - captions will skip the 'full video' link.")
77	        return {}
78	
79	    try:
80	        channel_resp = requests.get(f"{YOUTUBE_API_BASE}/channels", params={
81	            "part": "contentDetails",
82	            "forHandle": YOUTUBE_CHANNEL_HANDLE,
83	            "key": YOUTUBE_API_KEY,
84	        })
85	        channel_resp.raise_for_status()
86	        items = channel_resp.json().get("items", [])
87	        if not items:
88	            print(f"WARNING: No YouTube channel found for handle '{YOUTUBE_CHANNEL_HANDLE}'.")
89	            return {}
90	        uploads_playlist_id = items[0]["contentDetails"]["relatedPlaylists"]["uploads"]
91	
92	        video_map = {}
93	        page_token = None
94	        while True:
95	            params = {
96	                "part": "snippet",
97	                "playlistId": uploads_playlist_id,
98	                "maxResults": 50,
99	                "key": YOUTUBE_API_KEY,
100	            }
101	            if page_token:
102	                params["pageToken"] = page_token
103	            resp = requests.get(f"{YOUTUBE_API_BASE}/playlistItems", params=params)
104	            resp.raise_for_status()
105	            data = resp.json()
106	            for item in data.get("items", []):
107	                snippet = item["snippet"]
108	                video_id = snippet["resourceId"]["videoId"]
109	                video_map[snippet["title"]] = f"https://youtu.be/{video_id}"
110	            page_token = data.get("nextPageToken")
111	            if not page_token:
112	                break
113	    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
114	        print(f"WARNING: YouTube API lookup failed, captions will skip the link this run: {e}")
115	        return {}
116	
117	    with open(YOUTUBE_CACHE_FILE, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
118	        json.dump(video_map, f)
119	    return video_map

122	def load_youtube_overrides():
123	    overrides = {}
124	    if os.path.exists(YOUTUBE_OVERRIDES_FILE):
125	        with open(YOUTUBE_OVERRIDES_FILE, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
126	            for line in f:
127	                line = line.strip()
128	                if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
129	                    continue
130	                name, url = line.split("=", 1)
131	                overrides[name.strip()] = url.strip()
132	    return overrides
133	
134	
135	def match_youtube_url(source_video_title, video_map, overrides):
136	    """Returns (url, how_matched) so callers can log/verify what happened - a silent wrong
137	    fuzzy match (pointing viewers at the wrong video) is worse than no match at all."""
138	    if source_video_title in overrides:
139	        return overrides[source_video_title], "manual override"
140	    if source_video_title in video_map:
141	        return video_map[source_video_title], "exact title match"
142	    close = difflib.get_close_matches(source_video_title, video_map.keys(), n=1, cutoff=0.6)
143	    if close:
144	        return video_map[close[0]], f"fuzzy match against '{close[0]}'"
145	    return None, None

That warning just means the `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` placeholder in `poster.py` was never filled in — the script falls back to your manual override file when it can (which is what happened here), but any video *without* an override entry silently gets no "Full video" link at all.

To fix it:

1. Go to [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/), create (or pick) a project.
2. **APIs & Services → Library** → search "YouTube Data API v3" → **Enable**.
3. **APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → API key**.
4. Copy that key and paste it into `poster.py` at line 16, replacing the placeholder:
